pathway.title: TPG RE Finance Trust, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: TPG RE Finance Trust, Inc. grew its balance sheet with debt in 2026, and that is the finding that matters most. Debt principal rose from USD 3,309.5 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 4,198.1 million at 2026-09-30, while stockholders' equity fell from USD 1,068.0 million to USD 1,024.1 million, so the company's own total leverage ratio rose from 3.02x to 4.03x and the debt-to-equity ratio excluding the Term Loan B from 3.02x to 3.64x. The 10-K had said the company expected total debt to equity to be generally below 3.75:1. On the ratio that includes the Term Loan B, TRTX is above that range; reducing net debt by about USD 286.8 million, or adding about USD 76.5 million of equity, would bring it back to 3.75x. The basis of the 3.75:1 expectation after the Term Loan B is not stated, so this is a pointer, not a breach [Documentary Fact; CP-1: Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A: logged difference on leverage expectation].

The company's funding became more corporate and more recourse. A USD 400.0 million Term Loan B at Term SOFR plus 2.75% maturing in May 2033 and an undrawn USD 100.0 million Revolver closed in May 2026; both are fully recourse, as is the USD 265.0 million secured revolving facility. Together with partial recourse to Holdco on the secured credit agreements, nominal recourse exposure is USD 1,051.7 million, about 1.03 times equity, and the cash the company holds for its liquidity covenant, USD 52.6 million, is consistent with five percent of that exposure. Against this, 45.7% of debt is non-recourse CRE CLO debt and 78.8% is not subject to market-value margin calls [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Funding structure and recourse].

Liquidity improved in headline terms but is thin in usable terms. Near-term liquidity of USD 291.6 million at 2026-09-30 compares with USD 143.0 million at 2025-12-31, but USD 52.6 million of the USD 70.8 million of cash is held for covenants, and only USD 87.3 million of the USD 777.8 million of secured credit agreement availability counts as available without pledging more collateral. After covenant cash, liquidity of about USD 239.0 million is about equal to USD 236.6 million of unfunded loan commitments [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Liquidity].

Earnings softened in the latest quarter and cover of the dividend is below one after realized losses. Net income was USD 9.4 million in Q3 2026 against USD 22.0 million a year earlier, and net interest income fell 5.7%. Distributable Earnings before realized losses covered the common dividend 0.98 times in Q3 2026, but after the USD 13.0 million realized loss on a Plano foreclosure Distributable Earnings were USD 5.1 million against common dividends declared of USD 18.5 million, a cover of 0.28 times. Over nine months of 2026 they covered declared common dividends 0.98 times before and 0.75 times after realized losses, while the company also bought back shares for USD 24.6 million [Documentary Fact; CP-1: Earnings measures; CP-1A: Governance].

Asset quality indicators remain stable but the book is transitional and growing. Weighted average risk rating is 3.0, no loan was on non-accrual at 2026-09-30, and the allowance is 147 bp of commitments, or USD 76.1 million. Multifamily and industrial are 75.2% of commitments and loans are 99.7% floating rate. Offsetting this, 64.0% of commitments are bridge loans, seven real estate owned properties are held after a September 2026 foreclosure, and office exposure rose from 4.3% to 7.9% after a USD 212.0 million San Francisco loan, after management said in April 2026 that office exposure was below 5% [Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1: Credit quality; CP-1A: logged difference on office exposure].

Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2028 and depends on extensions. Debt maturing in 2028 is USD 1,130.8 million, 26.9% of principal, including USD 792.6 million of secured credit agreements and USD 265.0 million of the secured revolver; CLO maturities follow loan repayments. A USD 1.0 billion managed CRE CLO closed on 2026-10-02, after the balance sheet date, with about USD 820.0 million of investment-grade notes placed, but its use of proceeds is not disclosed, so its effect on leverage and recourse is unknown [Documentary Fact; CP-1: Chart data: debt maturities; CP-1A: Transaction summary].

runs.text: Strength: collateral quality indicators. The loan book is entirely senior first mortgage loans, with a weighted average risk rating of 3.0 unchanged since 2025-12-31, no non-accrual loans, a weighted average loan-to-value of 65.9% at origination and an allowance of 147 bp of commitments. The mechanism is that senior, floating-rate lending with interest rate floors protects income and gives asset-level lenders collateral cover; the implication is limited realized losses so far (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Credit quality). The loan-to-value is an underwriting measure, not a current valuation.

Strength: funding structure. 78.8% of debt is not subject to market-value margin calls, 45.7% is non-recourse CLO debt isolated from parent assets, the Term Loan B runs to May 2033 and the Revolver to May 2031, and secured credit agreement lenders are four banks. The mechanism is that forced deleveraging through margin calls is limited and term funding is long; the implication is lower exposure to market-value margin calls, although the secured credit agreements remain repurchase-style borrowings with credit marks (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Funding structure and recourse).

Strength: disclosure and interest rate positioning. The company publishes a loan-by-loan schedule, risk ratings, recourse by facility and a liquidity table, and a 25 bp rise in rates adds about USD 2.9 million to annual net interest income because net floating-rate exposure is USD 1,186.2 million. The implication is good monitorability and a positive rate sensitivity (Documentary Fact; CP-1A: Company and operating model).

Weakness: leverage and thin equity cushion. Total leverage of 4.03x is above the 10-K's 3.75:1 expectation, equity fell 4.1% in nine months, and the indicative ratio of debt principal to total assets is 80.1% against a covenant maximum of 83.333%; assets could fall by only about USD 205.2 million, or 3.9%, before that indicative ratio reaches the maximum. The mechanism is that realized and provisioned losses reduce equity directly while debt is fixed; the implication is limited tolerance for credit losses before covenant pressure, subject to the unsupplied covenant definition (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Covenants, Calculations).

Weakness: usable liquidity and lender discretion. Cash tied to covenants rises with each draw on recourse debt, secured credit agreement availability depends on lender-approved collateral, and unfunded commitments are USD 236.6 million. The mechanism is that liquidity can shrink when repayments slow or when the recourse base grows; the implication is dependence on repayments and the October 2026 CLO for headroom (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Liquidity).

Weakness: earnings cover and distributions. Dividends and buybacks exceeded earnings after realized losses in Q3 2026, and nine-month Distributable Earnings of USD 42.3 million were below declared common dividends of USD 56.7 million. The mechanism is that distributions drawn from equity reduce the cushion beneath creditors; the implication is that continued distributions at this level depend on earnings recovery (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Earnings measures).

Weakness: external management and affiliate arrangements. The manager earns 1.50% of Equity as defined regardless of performance, the fee base implied by the Q3 2026 fee exceeds stockholders' equity, three of eight directors are TPG employees and affiliate payments are disclosed but small. The mechanism is that the manager's income does not fall with credit losses; the implication is indirect alignment with creditors and no documented sponsor support (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A: Ownership and control, Governance).

Weakness: missing measures. EBITDA, covenant ratio values and executed agreements are not available, so leverage and coverage on lender definitions cannot be tested (Insufficient Information; limitation stated in the gaps).

runs.text: All items below are completed unless labelled as a subsequent event. There is no transaction source for a sponsor deal, merger or change of control, and none is inferred; the pack describes financing and portfolio activity only.

In May 2026 TRTX closed a 400.0 million secured Term Loan B at a price of 99.75, bearing Term SOFR plus 2.75%, maturing May 2033, with quarterly amortization of 0.25% of the original principal from the last business day of December 2026. Obligations are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries and secured on a first-priority basis by substantially all assets of the company and certain subsidiaries (10-Q Q3 page:56). The filing says the Term Loan B and the Revolver are used "to repay outstanding indebtedness and for other general corporate purposes" (page:55); which indebtedness was repaid is not itemized, although the Q3 filing links the May 2026 redemption of TRTX 2022-FL5 to an upsized Wells Fargo agreement (page:44). At the same time TRTX closed a 100.0 million Revolver at Term SOFR plus 2.00% maturing May 2031, undrawn at 2026-09-30 (page:57). A Credit Agreement dated 2026-05-14 with Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and other lenders is listed as an exhibit to the Q2 2026 10-Q (10-Q Q2 page:133); the filings do not say which facility it governs and the text is not supplied. The company also paid TPG Capital BD, an affiliate of TPG, 0.9 million for capital markets services on these facilities (10-Q Q3 page:65). The management characterised the closing as securing "highly durable, non-mark-to-market liquidity" (release 2026-07-28 page:2), which is Management Language; the Term Loan B and Revolver contain no margin calls, but they are fully recourse (CP-1 handoff).

Investment-portfolio financing also changed in 2026. On May 15, 2026 TRTX redeemed TRTX 2022-FL5, which had 597.8 million of investment-grade bonds outstanding, and refinanced 17 loans with an aggregate unpaid principal balance of 698.1 million primarily through the upsize of the Wells Fargo secured credit agreement (10-Q Q3 page:43-44). The Wells Fargo agreement was increased to 850.0 million and its maturity extended to May 12, 2028 on May 12, 2026, with no margin calls for one year from that date; the Goldman Sachs agreement was increased to 750.0 million on June 30, 2026; a new 500.0 million Citi agreement closed on June 30, 2026; the Bank of America maturity extension to June 6, 2029, executed in January 2026, took effect on June 6, 2026; and the Barclays agreement was allowed to expire on its initial maturity in May 2026 with no borrowings outstanding (page:48). In September 2026 a 29.1 million first mortgage loan from BMO Harris Bank on the Plano multifamily property replaced an asset-specific financing after the underlying loan converted to real estate owned through a non-judicial foreclosure on September 1, 2026, which crystallized a 13.0 million realized loss (page:39, page:54).

After the quarter, as a subsequent event, TRTX closed TRTX 2026-FL8, a 1.0 billion managed CRE CLO, on October 2, 2026, placing approximately 820.0 million of investment-grade securities with institutional investors (10-Q Q3 page:74; release 2026-10-26 page:4). Supporting exhibits (indenture, collateral interest purchase agreement, collateral management agreement and servicing agreement) were filed with an 8-K of October 6, 2026 that is not in the pack (page:135). The use of proceeds, the collateral, the retained interest, any related redemption of other debt and the effect on the secured credit agreements are not stated. The liquidity effect of the CLO cannot be assessed; the 2026-09-30 balance sheet does not include it. Also as a subsequent event, repayments of 72.2 million were received, including a full repayment of 61.5 million (page:74), and on October 26, 2026 the board approved a new share repurchase program of up to 50.0 million of common stock, which management described as "doubling our prior authorization" (release 2026-10-26 page:2); this is Management Language, and the prior authorization was a 25.0 million program announced on September 4, 2025 (10-Q Q2 page:132). Repurchases in 9M 2026 retired 3,021,254 shares for 24,613 thousand of cash (10-Q Q3 page:8-10; Calculations).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial base is sufficient to support a credit snapshot of TRTX on a reported basis, with the limits stated here. TRTX is a floating-rate commercial real estate lender: 99.7% of loan commitments are floating rate (10-Q Q3 page:31), and loans held for investment of 4,916,375 thousand at amortized cost make up most of total assets of 5,242,861 thousand (page:6-7). There is no EBITDA, so the chart selectors for EBITDA leverage and cover are recorded as Not supplied and the leverage and cover analysis is built on the company's own debt-to-equity and total leverage ratios, on debt principal against equity, and on interest income against interest expense.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main story is balance sheet growth funded with debt. Total debt principal grew from 3,309,462 thousand at 2025-12-31 to 4,198,054 thousand at 2026-09-30 (10-Q Q3 page:89), an increase of 888,592 thousand, while total stockholders' equity fell from 1,068,023 thousand to 1,024,126 thousand (page:7). The company's own total leverage ratio, debt including the Term Loan B less cash over equity, rose from 3.02x to 4.03x (page:104-105). Most of the increase came in Q3 2026: the same ratio was 3.10x at 2026-03-31 and 3.32x at 2026-06-30 (10-Q Q1 page:93; 10-Q Q2 page:102). Funding changed in kind as well as in size: the 2022 CLO was redeemed in May 2026 (page:43), and funding moved to larger secured credit agreements with Wells Fargo, Citi and Goldman Sachs, a secured revolver drawn to 264,963 thousand, and a new 400,000 thousand Term Loan B that is fully recourse (page:56, page:89). The share of debt that is non-recourse CLO debt fell from 78.4% at 2025-12-31 to 45.7% at 2026-09-30 (page:77, page:89).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are lower and thinner than in 2025. Net interest income was 76,067 thousand in 9M 2026 against 78,334 thousand in 9M 2025, because interest expense grew by 17,019 thousand while interest income grew by 14,752 thousand (page:7-8, page:102). Credit loss expense was 11,850 thousand in 9M 2026 against 2,594 thousand in 9M 2025. Net income was 41,437 thousand against 56,343 thousand. Q3 2026 was the weakest quarter: net income 9,366 thousand against 21,993 thousand in Q3 2025, credit loss expense 8,573 thousand, and Distributable Earnings of 5,118 thousand after a 13,006 thousand realized loss on a Plano multifamily foreclosure (page:39, page:81). Distributable Earnings before realized losses were 18,124 thousand against a common dividend declared of 18,508 thousand (release 2026-10-26 page:8). Loan credit metrics are otherwise stable on the face of the filing: weighted average risk rating 3.0 unchanged, no loan on non-accrual at 2026-09-30 compared with one of 41.0 million at 2025-12-31, and an allowance of 147 basis points of total commitments (page:34, page:37, page:88). The quality of the book changed in one respect worth carrying forward: office exposure was 4.3% of commitments at 2026-06-30 and 7.9% at 2026-09-30 after a 212.0 million San Francisco office loan was originated on 2026-09-24 (10-Q Q2 page:71; 10-Q Q3 page:72, page:116). The Q1 2026 release had said office exposure was below 5% (release 2026-04-28 page:2); that was a management statement about a point in time and does not describe 2026-09-30.

Near-term liquidity of 291,634 thousand at 2026-09-30 includes 70,826 thousand of cash of which 52.6 million is held to satisfy liquidity covenants (page:28, page:77, page:105). Unfunded loan commitments are 236,552 thousand (page:71). The covenant package changed when the Term Loan B and Revolver closed (page:55): the investment-portfolio debt-to-equity covenant of 4.25x is shown as not applicable currently, a total debt to total assets maximum of 83.333% applies, and the interest coverage minimum fell from 1.4x to 1.3x. The company states it was in compliance with all financial covenants (page:55, page:57), but the actual test values are not printed, so no headroom is reported as a company figure; an indicative balance sheet debt to assets ratio is set out in Calculations with its caveats.

fields.value: The recourse layer matters more than any single ratio. Applying the printed recourse percentages to principal gives nominal recourse exposure of 1,051,727 thousand at 2026-09-30 (Calculations), made up of 664,963 thousand of fully recourse debt and 386,764 thousand of partial recourse. Five percent of that, 52,586 thousand, is consistent with the 52.6 million of cash the company reports holding for the liquidity covenant (page:28). The same test is consistent with the 39.5 million held at 2026-06-30 (release 2026-07-28 page:3) and gives a requirement below the 15.0 million floor at 2025-12-31 (page:28) and 2026-03-31 (release 2026-04-28 page:3), when 15.0 million was held. This suggests the company holds cash at the covenant minimum and that required cash rises with each draw on recourse debt. The filing does not define "recourse indebtedness" and the match holds only on the basis chosen in Calculations, so it is an inference.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Near-term liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 291,634 thousand as the issuer defines it (page:105). It excludes contractual availability that depends on lender-approved collateral. Three points qualify the headline. First, 52.6 million of the 70,826 thousand cash is held for liquidity covenants (page:28), leaving 18.2 million available for investment (page:77). Second, the 87,317 thousand of secured credit agreement capacity is defined as available without pledging additional collateral (page:77), while maximum current availability is 777,844 thousand (page:47). Third, the 22,000 thousand secured revolver figure compares with an undrawn commitment of 110.0 million (375.0 million less 265.0 million drawn, page:77); collateral eligibility limits the difference. Against these, the company has unfunded loan commitments of 236,552 thousand (page:71), of which 26,740 thousand fall due within a year (page:108), and unencumbered loans of 187.2 million that can be pledged (page:106). Contractual obligations due in less than one year are 3,000 thousand of Term Loan B principal and 26,740 thousand of unfunded commitments, plus estimated interest, for a printed total of 272,285 thousand (page:108). The secured credit agreement and secured revolver maturities used in the schedule fall in 2028 or later (page:57), so no facility is shown expiring within twelve months of the as-of date.

No external material is used; nothing in this handoff comes from outside the pinned sources. The context names no sponsor, parent, borrower, guarantor, deal terms or research questions; those blanks are treated as not supplied. The filings do describe TPG as the sponsor of the external manager, so the sponsor fact comes from the filings, not the context.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TRTX is a REIT that originates and acquires floating-rate commercial real estate first mortgage loans, financed mainly by CRE CLOs, secured credit agreements and, since May 2026, a corporate Term Loan B and Revolver. It has no employees; its Manager, TPG RE Finance Trust Management, L.P., an affiliate of TPG, runs the business under a Management Agreement, and the chief executive officer, president and interim chief financial officer are TPG Real Estate professionals (10-K page:7-8, page:17). The creditor-relevant structure is therefore a levered, externally managed lender: income is the spread between floating-rate loan interest and floating-rate funding cost, protected in part by interest rate floors on the loans, and creditor protection depends on collateral quality, on how much of the funding is non-recourse or non-marked, and on how a manager paid on equity behaves as leverage grows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction story is a refinancing and liability-management story, not a sponsor transaction. In the quarter ended 2026-06-30 the company closed a 400.0 million Term Loan B and a 100.0 million Revolver, upsized the Wells Fargo and Goldman Sachs secured credit agreements, closed a new 500.0 million Citi secured credit agreement, let the Barclays agreement lapse and redeemed the 2022 CLO (TRTX 2022-FL5) (10-Q Q3 page:43-44, page:48, page:55-57). After quarter end it closed a 1.0 billion managed CRE CLO, TRTX 2026-FL8, on 2026-10-02 and approved a new 50.0 million share repurchase program on 2026-10-26 (10-Q Q3 page:74). There is no change of control, no acquisition of TRTX and no sponsor equity injection in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the financial side, which comes from the accepted financial base and is not recomputed here, debt principal rose to 4,198,054 thousand at 2026-09-30 and the issuer's total leverage ratio to 4.03x, with liquidity of 291,634 thousand against unfunded loan commitments of 236,552 thousand (CP-1 handoff). Against that, the business has stable reported credit indicators: weighted average risk rating 3.0 unchanged, no loan on non-accrual at 2026-09-30, and an allowance of 147 basis points of commitments (10-Q Q3 page:34, page:37, page:88). The main business-model risks are the combination of rising leverage with continued buybacks and dividends, the concentration of refinancing in 2028, the dependence on lender discretion for secured credit agreement availability, and the manager conflicts described below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In May 2026 TRTX closed a 400.0 million secured Term Loan B at a price of 99.75, bearing Term SOFR plus 2.75%, maturing May 2033, with quarterly amortization of 0.25% of the original principal from the last business day of December 2026. Obligations are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries and secured on a first-priority basis by substantially all assets of the company and certain subsidiaries (10-Q Q3 page:56). The filing says the Term Loan B and the Revolver are used "to repay outstanding indebtedness and for other general corporate purposes" (page:55); which indebtedness was repaid is not itemized, although the Q3 filing links the May 2026 redemption of TRTX 2022-FL5 to an upsized Wells Fargo agreement (page:44). At the same time TRTX closed a 100.0 million Revolver at Term SOFR plus 2.00% maturing May 2031, undrawn at 2026-09-30 (page:57). A Credit Agreement dated 2026-05-14 with Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and other lenders is listed as an exhibit to the Q2 2026 10-Q (10-Q Q2 page:133); the filings do not say which facility it governs and the text is not supplied. The company also paid TPG Capital BD, an affiliate of TPG, 0.9 million for capital markets services on these facilities (10-Q Q3 page:65). The management characterised the closing as securing "highly durable, non-mark-to-market liquidity" (release 2026-07-28 page:2), which is Management Language; the Term Loan B and Revolver contain no margin calls, but they are fully recourse (CP-1 handoff).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Investment-portfolio financing also changed in 2026. On May 15, 2026 TRTX redeemed TRTX 2022-FL5, which had 597.8 million of investment-grade bonds outstanding, and refinanced 17 loans with an aggregate unpaid principal balance of 698.1 million primarily through the upsize of the Wells Fargo secured credit agreement (10-Q Q3 page:43-44). The Wells Fargo agreement was increased to 850.0 million and its maturity extended to May 12, 2028 on May 12, 2026, with no margin calls for one year from that date; the Goldman Sachs agreement was increased to 750.0 million on June 30, 2026; a new 500.0 million Citi agreement closed on June 30, 2026; the Bank of America maturity extension to June 6, 2029, executed in January 2026, took effect on June 6, 2026; and the Barclays agreement was allowed to expire on its initial maturity in May 2026 with no borrowings outstanding (page:48). In September 2026 a 29.1 million first mortgage loan from BMO Harris Bank on the Plano multifamily property replaced an asset-specific financing after the underlying loan converted to real estate owned through a non-judicial foreclosure on September 1, 2026, which crystallized a 13.0 million realized loss (page:39, page:54).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the quarter, as a subsequent event, TRTX closed TRTX 2026-FL8, a 1.0 billion managed CRE CLO, on October 2, 2026, placing approximately 820.0 million of investment-grade securities with institutional investors (10-Q Q3 page:74; release 2026-10-26 page:4). Supporting exhibits (indenture, collateral interest purchase agreement, collateral management agreement and servicing agreement) were filed with an 8-K of October 6, 2026 that is not in the pack (page:135). The use of proceeds, the collateral, the retained interest, any related redemption of other debt and the effect on the secured credit agreements are not stated. The liquidity effect of the CLO cannot be assessed; the 2026-09-30 balance sheet does not include it. Also as a subsequent event, repayments of 72.2 million were received, including a full repayment of 61.5 million (page:74), and on October 26, 2026 the board approved a new share repurchase program of up to 50.0 million of common stock, which management described as "doubling our prior authorization" (release 2026-10-26 page:2); this is Management Language, and the prior authorization was a 25.0 million program announced on September 4, 2025 (10-Q Q2 page:132). Repurchases in 9M 2026 retired 3,021,254 shares for 24,613 thousand of cash (10-Q Q3 page:8-10; Calculations).

fields.value: This synthesis covers TPG RE Finance Trust, Inc. as of 2026-11-05 for the credit_snapshot pathway. It states the fundamental credit view from the accepted financial base and the business and transaction fact pack, in USD, with Q3 2026 as the current period and FY2025 as the prior period.

fields.value: The synthesis works from the upstream handoffs, whose figures and locators come from the issuer sources below. Locators in brackets name the handoff section; the page locators are those given in the handoffs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TPG RE Finance Trust, Inc. is a moderately leveraged, externally managed commercial real estate lender whose asset quality looks stable but whose cushions are narrowing. The strongest support is a senior, floating-rate loan book with a weighted average risk rating of 3.0, no non-accrual loans and commitments of USD 5,168.7 million, funded 78.8% without market-value margin calls. The weakest point is leverage: debt of USD 4,198.1 million against equity of USD 1,024.1 million gives 4.03x, above the 3.75:1 the company expected in its 10-K, with USD 52.6 million of cash tied up for covenants. What decides the outcome is whether loan repayments and the October 2026 CLO bring leverage and liquidity back toward the company's own range while earnings cover the dividend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The lender's senior, floating-rate, mostly multifamily and industrial loan book and long-dated, largely non-marked funding support its credit quality, but a rise in leverage to 4.03x, thin usable liquidity and dividend cover below one after realized losses leave a narrowing cushion that depends on repayments and refinancing execution through 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TPG RE Finance Trust, Inc. grew its balance sheet with debt in 2026, and that is the finding that matters most. Debt principal rose from USD 3,309.5 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 4,198.1 million at 2026-09-30, while stockholders' equity fell from USD 1,068.0 million to USD 1,024.1 million, so the company's own total leverage ratio rose from 3.02x to 4.03x and the debt-to-equity ratio excluding the Term Loan B from 3.02x to 3.64x. The 10-K had said the company expected total debt to equity to be generally below 3.75:1. On the ratio that includes the Term Loan B, TRTX is above that range; reducing net debt by about USD 286.8 million, or adding about USD 76.5 million of equity, would bring it back to 3.75x. The basis of the 3.75:1 expectation after the Term Loan B is not stated, so this is a pointer, not a breach [Documentary Fact; CP-1: Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A: logged difference on leverage expectation].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company's funding became more corporate and more recourse. A USD 400.0 million Term Loan B at Term SOFR plus 2.75% maturing in May 2033 and an undrawn USD 100.0 million Revolver closed in May 2026; both are fully recourse, as is the USD 265.0 million secured revolving facility. Together with partial recourse to Holdco on the secured credit agreements, nominal recourse exposure is USD 1,051.7 million, about 1.03 times equity, and the cash the company holds for its liquidity covenant, USD 52.6 million, is consistent with five percent of that exposure. Against this, 45.7% of debt is non-recourse CRE CLO debt and 78.8% is not subject to market-value margin calls [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Funding structure and recourse].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity improved in headline terms but is thin in usable terms. Near-term liquidity of USD 291.6 million at 2026-09-30 compares with USD 143.0 million at 2025-12-31, but USD 52.6 million of the USD 70.8 million of cash is held for covenants, and only USD 87.3 million of the USD 777.8 million of secured credit agreement availability counts as available without pledging more collateral. After covenant cash, liquidity of about USD 239.0 million is about equal to USD 236.6 million of unfunded loan commitments [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Liquidity].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings softened in the latest quarter and cover of the dividend is below one after realized losses. Net income was USD 9.4 million in Q3 2026 against USD 22.0 million a year earlier, and net interest income fell 5.7%. Distributable Earnings before realized losses covered the common dividend 0.98 times in Q3 2026, but after the USD 13.0 million realized loss on a Plano foreclosure Distributable Earnings were USD 5.1 million against common dividends declared of USD 18.5 million, a cover of 0.28 times. Over nine months of 2026 they covered declared common dividends 0.98 times before and 0.75 times after realized losses, while the company also bought back shares for USD 24.6 million [Documentary Fact; CP-1: Earnings measures; CP-1A: Governance].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Asset quality indicators remain stable but the book is transitional and growing. Weighted average risk rating is 3.0, no loan was on non-accrual at 2026-09-30, and the allowance is 147 bp of commitments, or USD 76.1 million. Multifamily and industrial are 75.2% of commitments and loans are 99.7% floating rate. Offsetting this, 64.0% of commitments are bridge loans, seven real estate owned properties are held after a September 2026 foreclosure, and office exposure rose from 4.3% to 7.9% after a USD 212.0 million San Francisco loan, after management said in April 2026 that office exposure was below 5% [Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1: Credit quality; CP-1A: logged difference on office exposure].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2028 and depends on extensions. Debt maturing in 2028 is USD 1,130.8 million, 26.9% of principal, including USD 792.6 million of secured credit agreements and USD 265.0 million of the secured revolver; CLO maturities follow loan repayments. A USD 1.0 billion managed CRE CLO closed on 2026-10-02, after the balance sheet date, with about USD 820.0 million of investment-grade notes placed, but its use of proceeds is not disclosed, so its effect on leverage and recourse is unknown [Documentary Fact; CP-1: Chart data: debt maturities; CP-1A: Transaction summary].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: collateral quality indicators. The loan book is entirely senior first mortgage loans, with a weighted average risk rating of 3.0 unchanged since 2025-12-31, no non-accrual loans, a weighted average loan-to-value of 65.9% at origination and an allowance of 147 bp of commitments. The mechanism is that senior, floating-rate lending with interest rate floors protects income and gives asset-level lenders collateral cover; the implication is limited realized losses so far (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Credit quality). The loan-to-value is an underwriting measure, not a current valuation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: funding structure. 78.8% of debt is not subject to market-value margin calls, 45.7% is non-recourse CLO debt isolated from parent assets, the Term Loan B runs to May 2033 and the Revolver to May 2031, and secured credit agreement lenders are four banks. The mechanism is that forced deleveraging through margin calls is limited and term funding is long; the implication is lower exposure to market-value margin calls, although the secured credit agreements remain repurchase-style borrowings with credit marks (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Funding structure and recourse).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: disclosure and interest rate positioning. The company publishes a loan-by-loan schedule, risk ratings, recourse by facility and a liquidity table, and a 25 bp rise in rates adds about USD 2.9 million to annual net interest income because net floating-rate exposure is USD 1,186.2 million. The implication is good monitorability and a positive rate sensitivity (Documentary Fact; CP-1A: Company and operating model).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: leverage and thin equity cushion. Total leverage of 4.03x is above the 10-K's 3.75:1 expectation, equity fell 4.1% in nine months, and the indicative ratio of debt principal to total assets is 80.1% against a covenant maximum of 83.333%; assets could fall by only about USD 205.2 million, or 3.9%, before that indicative ratio reaches the maximum. The mechanism is that realized and provisioned losses reduce equity directly while debt is fixed; the implication is limited tolerance for credit losses before covenant pressure, subject to the unsupplied covenant definition (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Covenants, Calculations).

Dividends and buybacks exceeded earnings after realized losses in Q3 2026, and nine-month Distributable Earnings of USD 42.3 million were below declared common dividends of USD 56.7 million. The mechanism is that distributions drawn from equity reduce the cushion beneath creditors; the implication is that continued distributions at this level depend on earnings recovery (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Earnings measures).

The mechanism is that the manager's income does not fall with credit losses; the implication is indirect alignment with creditors and no documented sponsor support (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A: Ownership and control, Governance).
